chunks: Another text: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal; and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bizanti, from Abu Ali al-Khazzar, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim - that is Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) - 'May my father be your ransom! I have grown old and I fear that something might happen to me and I will not be able to meet you, so inform me who is the Imam after you?' He said: 'My son, Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.فِدَاكَ أَبِي: May my father be your ransom (a term of deep respect)

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam Musa al-Kadhim appoint as his successor?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the explicit designation (naṣṣ) of Imam Ali al-Rida (s) by his father, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (s), addressing the Shia concern of *ghaybat al-imam* (absence of the Imam) during periods of political turmoil. The direct answer underscores the continuity of the Imamate within the progeny of Imam al-Kadim, reinforcing the doctrine of *nass* as the primary mechanism for succession in Twelver Shi'ism.
